Every gap request and repair control that reaches an origin is admitted through its durable outbound worker. An admission that loses the held message's version fence, usually a request's gap half to its own repair half, goes `pending-control` and is expedited into the batch already running, ahead of the claims that batch holds and without counting toward its page, so on a slow store one batch ran 15 to 25 s. What its controls cause waits for that batch to end: the retries of pending gap requests after their three expedited runs, the repair hints a committed repair writes and the repair sends. Whether the cell passes depends on where the long batch falls relative to the origin's waits, not on the runner's speed; nothing is lost, and renewals stop at request 4. The wait also matched exactly request 3, although a later request can commit first; pull request 907 removes only that assumption, accepting request 3 or any later one, and the cell stays intermittently red until the work handler bounds a running batch. Observation run 45690968763 on main 99016dc5a (41.88 ms/op) failed relayed-unreceipted-gap-renewal. With a 50 s lifetime and a 25 s hold, since withdrawn, runs 45707321821 (29.04 ms/op) and 45707356002 (39.24 ms/op) failed both cells and run 45707352091 (38.6 ms/op) passed; the long batch appeared in all three.
